facts.claim: Closing a side-panel/scene-panel state must account for two independent reducers: `sceneLayoutLogic.scenePanelOpenManual` (manual toggle) and `sidePanelStateLogic.sidePanelOpen`/`selectedTab` (the Info tab route); `sceneLayoutLogic.scenePanelOpen` is a selector combining both (`scenePanelOpenManual || (sidePanelOpen && selectedTab === SidePanelTab.Info)`). A listener that wants to force the panel closed after an action (e.g. duplicating an insight) must call both `sceneLayoutLogic.actions.setScenePanelOpen(false)` and `sidePanelStateLogic.actions.closeSidePanel()`, or it leaves the panel open through the other path.
facts.evidence: `frontend/src/layout/scenes/sceneLayoutLogic.tsx`: `scenePanelOpen: [(s) => [s.scenePanelOpenManual, s.sidePanelOpen, s.selectedTab], (...) => scenePanelOpenManual || (sidePanelOpen && selectedTab === SidePanelTab.Info)]`; test added at `insightLogic.test.ts` mounts both logics and asserts `scenePanelOpenManual` and `sidePanelOpen` are both false after `duplicateInsight`.

facts.claim: `urls.resourceTransfer('Insight', insight.id!)` and `ResourceTransfer`'s back-link builder take the insight's numeric DB `id`, not its `short_id`; insight view/edit URLs (`urls.insightView`, `urls.insightEdit`) are keyed by `short_id`. Any back-link or navigation built from the resource-transfer scene for an Insight resource must resolve the short_id first (e.g. via `insightsApi.getByNumericId` then reading `.short_id`) before constructing `urls.insightView(...)` — passing the numeric id directly opens a nonexistent/wrong insight.
facts.evidence: `frontend/src/scenes/resource-transfer/ResourceTransfer.tsx` originally: `case 'Insight': return urls.insightView(resourceId as InsightShortId)` where `resourceId` was actually the numeric `insight.id`; fix added `sourceInsightShortId` loader state in `resourceTransferLogic.ts` (`loadSourceInsightShortId` via `insightsApi.getByNumericId(numericId)`) and only renders `forceBackTo` once resolved.

facts.claim: Container queries (`@container`, `@min-[Nrem]`, `@max-[Nrem]`), not viewport breakpoints (`md:`/`lg:`), are the required mechanism for making a shared component adapt to a narrow parent (e.g. a modal card) per Rule 6 in `frontend/src/AGENTS.md`; `LemonBanner.tsx` and `ProductEmptyState.tsx` are the reference implementations (`@container`, `@min-[64rem]/product-empty-state:grid-cols-...`).
facts.evidence: `frontend/src/AGENTS.md` Rule 6: "Break on the container, not the viewport... `lib/lemon-ui/LemonBanner/LemonBanner.tsx` is the pattern." Grep confirmed usage in `ProductEmptyState.tsx` (`@container/product-empty-state`, `@min-[64rem]/product-empty-state:grid-cols-...`) and `LemonBanner.tsx` (`'LemonBanner @container'`).

All three required multiple greps/reads across files to establish and are concrete enough to act on directly. Did not include file-inventory or other task-specific details."
